content.snl: thm-hyp(list-partial(Type.judge(@F, Analysis.PFun), Type.judge(@x, Real), Type.judge(@N, Nat), $#0 > 0$(N)), Logic.exists-typed(@R, Analysis.PFun, Logic.and(Eq(F, Add.add(Analysis.taylorPoly(F, x, N), R)), Analysis.higherInfinitesimal(R, Power(Sub.sub(@y, x), N), x))))
content.markdown:
If `F` is `N`-times differentiable at `x₀` then `F` splits as its Taylor polynomial plus a remainder that is `o((x − x₀)ᴺ)` at `x₀`.

This is a purely local statement: it says the polynomial is the best degree-`N` approximation *near* `x₀` and says nothing at any fixed distance. It requires only differentiability at the single point `x₀`, which is the weakest hypothesis of any Taylor result here, and it is the form used for computing limits.
